note: Leads are not verified parsers. Ranks are assigned only among verified paths.

leads.name: sqlparse
leads.reason: sqlparse.parse returns grouped Statement token trees; non-validating parser (see catalog/sql/PROTOCOL.md).

leads.name: sqlglot
leads.reason: sqlglot.parse / parse_one return an Expression AST (exp.Select, exp.Insert); dialect selectable.

leads.name: sqlfluff
leads.family: sqlfluff lexer and dialect grammar matcher
leads.reason: sqlfluff.parse(sql, dialect="ansi") is a documented parse API that returns the full segment parse tree as nested records; it raises APIParsingError on unparsable input. Both valid controls equal the oracle (round 2).

leads.name: pglast
leads.family: PostgreSQL grammar (libpg_query extraction of the PostgreSQL server parser)
leads.reason: pglast.parse_sql runs the vendored libpg_query 18.1.0 raw parser and converts the C tree into pglast.ast nodes in its own Cython layer. Both valid controls equal the oracle; source-built with LLVM coverage (round 2). Shared libpg_query family.

leads.name: sql-metadata
leads.reason: Re-checked in round 2: sql-metadata 3.0.1 depends on sqlglot>=30.12,<31 (not sqlparse, as recorded in round 1) and Parser(sql) exposes metadata only: query_type, tables, columns, columns_dict, columns_aliases, tables_aliases, values and values_dict. On controls/sql/select-join.sql it reports tables ['customers', 'orders'] and columns_dict select ['customers.region', 'orders.total', '*'], but no join count, no function names and no SELECT literals, so the protocol summary cannot be read from its documented API; reading its private sqlglot tree would be the selected sqlglot path. Excluded as a metadata wrapper over the sqlglot family, not padded under the Parsel precedent.

leads.name: sqlglotrs
leads.reason: Optional Rust tokenizer for sqlglot; not a separate parser API.

leads.name: sqllineage
leads.reason: Round-2 extension lead (PyPI Stats last_month 1,022,544, captured 2026-11-17). SQL lineage analyser that depends on sqlparse and sqlfluff (both selected) and reports source/target tables and column lineage, not a statement tree with the protocol summary. Excluded as a wrapper.

leads.name: sql-formatter
leads.reason: Formatter; no syntax tree.

leads.name: sqloxide
leads.reason: sqloxide.parse_sql(sql, dialect="generic") calls sqlparser 0.61.0 Parser::parse_sql and pythonizes the AST. Both valid controls equal the oracle; source-built with Rust coverage (round 2). Shared sqlparser-rs family.

leads.name: moz-sql-parser
leads.reason: Superseded name of mo-sql-parsing.

leads.name: sqlvalidator
leads.reason: Round-2 extension lead (PyPI Stats last_month 104,072, captured 2026-11-17). sqlvalidator.parse(text).sql_query builds a SelectStatement tree for controls/sql/select-join.sql, but its SQLStatementParser raises ParsingError on controls/sql/insert-values.sql (it parses SELECT statements only), so the fixed second control fails.

leads.name: mo-sql-parsing
leads.family: mo-sql-parsing grammar on the mo-parsing engine
leads.reason: mo_sql_parsing.parse returns a JSON parse tree from its grammar on the mo-parsing engine. Both valid controls equal the oracle (round 2).

leads.name: simple-ddl-parser
leads.reason: DDL-only parser, confirmed in round 2: simple-ddl-parser 1.13.0 DDLParser(text, silent=True).run() returns [] for both controls/sql/select-join.sql and controls/sql/insert-values.sql (no statement is recognised), so it cannot give the SELECT or INSERT summary.

leads.name: pg-query-python
leads.family: PostgreSQL grammar (libpg_query extraction of the PostgreSQL server parser)
leads.reason: Round 3: not a pinned parser source. pg-query-python 0.1.3 ships no libpg_query sources: its sdist (88 kB) setup.py runs 'git clone --depth 1 --branch $LIBPG_QUERY_TAG' (default the moving branch 16-latest) of github.com/pganalyze/libpg_query at build time, and its wheels bundle a prebuilt libpg_query.so whose libpg_query tag is recorded nowhere in the package (the package __version__ string is 17.0.0 while setup.py defaults to 16-latest). The parser source therefore cannot be pinned by the package, the ground on which psqlparse was also left unresolved; source coverage of a self-chosen libpg_query tag would not establish what the published wheels run. The ctypes binding and protobuf decoding are pinned, but they are not the parser.

leads.name: psqlparse
leads.family: PostgreSQL grammar (libpg_query extraction of the PostgreSQL server parser)
leads.reason: psqlparse 0.2.5 (2016 sdist, SHA-256 b8beb4b389e6e3738bae19a48d4c2798124f464ab40c94b907bb2a3fda4c1d33) does not vendor its parser: build_libpg_query.sh downloads the moving libpg_query 9.5-latest branch archive at build time, so the parser source cannot be pinned by the package. A build attempt on Ubuntu (Python 3.14, gcc, bison, flex, unzip) downloaded that archive (SHA-256 ef18100add8d09e0450eefd4488a4c0c6174975a72058e9ac654ac66ecf467ee on 2026-11-17) and then failed compiling PostgreSQL 9.5's c.h: "'bool' cannot be defined via 'typedef'" (C23 default), so the extension was not built. No pinned, buildable path.

leads.name: sqltree
leads.reason: sqltree 0.3.0 (2022; no license field in its PyPI metadata) rejects both controls as given: sqltree.api.sqltree(text) raises TokenizeError('unexpected character ;') on the statement terminator that both controls end with, and the package has no documented statement splitter. With the terminator removed by hand it builds Select and Insert nodes, but the harness may not rewrite the control. Stays a lead with that evidence.

leads.name: psqlparse2
leads.family: PostgreSQL grammar (libpg_query extraction of the PostgreSQL server parser)
leads.reason: Round-2 lead (PyPI Stats last_month 3,025), evaluated in round 3. psqlparse2.query_to_pb runs the Cython wrapper over its vendored libpg_query 16-5.1.0 (PostgreSQL 16.1 grammar) and decodes the protobuf into its generated pg_query_pb2 messages; both valid controls equal the oracle. Source-built from the pinned sdist with LLVM coverage (1,897 lines in 43 files, 1,240 in libpg_query); the AFL++ bridge maps wrapper and grammar/scanner/raw_parser regions (215 tuples and 228 features differ between controls). Shared libpg_query family with pglast; own wrapper and an older vendored release.

leads.name: pg-query
leads.family: PostgreSQL grammar (libpg_query extraction of the PostgreSQL server parser)
leads.reason: pg_query 0.29 (2018, Lele Gaifax) is the predecessor PyPI name of pglast; its own description says the package was renamed to pglast and superseded. Excluded as a predecessor rename (trust-dns-proto precedent); pglast is the selected path and the two metrics are not combined.

leads.name: sqlparser
leads.reason: Round-2 hit of the 'sqlpars' query (PyPI Stats last_month 2,053), checked in round 3. The 0.0.9 wheel's single module SqlParser.py imports jaydebeapi and pandas, splits SQL files on a '--:--' comment marker into setup, extract and cleanup strings and runs them over a JDBC connection; it builds no syntax tree, and running statements against a database is outside the protocol. The wheel has no licence text (License: UNKNOWN; LGPL only as a classifier).

leads.name: polyglot-sql
leads.reason: Round-3 hit of the 'polyglot-sql' query (PyPI Stats last_month 9,851, captured 2026-11-18). polyglot_sql.parse runs the polyglot-sql Rust parser through the package's pyo3 binding and returns Expression objects; both valid controls equal the oracle. Source-built from the pinned sdist with Rust coverage (2,994 parser-crate lines in 11 files, 218 binding lines); the AFL++ bridge gives 5,724 tuples and the controls differ by 2,574 tuples. Same polyglot-sql 0.14.1 crate source as the Rust polyglot-sql path (shared family).

leads.name: bigquery-sql-parser
leads.reason: Round-3 hit of the 'sql-pars' query (PyPI Stats last_month 8,116, captured 2026-11-18). 0.1.4 (2022, single py2.py3 wheel) splits the text with regular expressions: Query exposes columns from a regex over the SELECT list and full_table_ids from a FROM/JOIN pattern that requires project.dataset.table names; there is no join, function, predicate, grouping or literal structure and no INSERT support, so it cannot give the summary (same ground as marcocesarato/sqlparser in the PHP cell).

leads.name: mindsdb-sql
leads.reason: Round-3 hit of the 'mindsdb-sql' query (PyPI Stats last_month 7,674, captured 2026-11-18). Predecessor package of mindsdb-sql-parser: GPL-3.0, last release 0.21.0 (2024-11-14) with a sqlalchemy dependency, superseded by the MIT mindsdb_sql_parser repository of the same organisation; 63.9% of mindsdb_sql_parser 0.13.8's non-comment source lines (multiset) occur in mindsdb_sql 0.21.0. Predecessor names are not counted (pg_query/pglast and moz-sql-parser/mo-sql-parsing precedent); its metric is not combined with the successor's.

leads.name: mindsdb-sql-parser
leads.reason: Round-3 hit of the 'sql-pars' query (PyPI Stats last_month 2,499, captured 2026-11-18). mindsdb_sql_parser.parse_sql runs its SLY lexer and LALR grammar into its own AST (Select, Insert, Join, Function, Constant); both valid controls equal the oracle. Pure-Python sdist (no wheel) installed byte-identical; Python line tracing covers 1,820 lines in mindsdb_sql_parser and its vendored SLY; the AFL++ line bridge gives 1,805 tuples and the controls differ by 170 tuples. Independent family; mindsdb-sql is its excluded predecessor.

leads.name: twsqlparser
leads.reason: Round-3 hit of the 'sqlparser' query (PyPI Stats last_month 419, captured 2026-11-18). Two-way SQL template expander (README in the 1.0.4 wheel: builds dynamic SQL from SQL files by expanding comment directives and parameters, and returns SQL text without validating it); no statement tree, so it cannot give the summary.

leads.name: antlr-tsql
leads.family: antlr-tsql ANTLR 4 T-SQL grammar with antlr-ast tree shaping
leads.reason: Round-3 lead (PyPI Stats last_month 126, captured 2026-11-18). antlr_tsql.ast.parse runs the ANTLR 4 generated T-SQL parser on the antlr4 Python runtime and shapes the tree with antlr-ast; both valid controls equal the oracle (constant Terminals classified by their quotes). Built from pinned sdists; Python line tracing covers 2,893 lines of antlr_tsql, antlr-ast and the antlr4 runtime; the AFL++ line bridge gives 2,851 tuples and the controls differ by 1,219 tuples. Independent family; very weak metric.
